item.title: Drive Radio — August 6, 2026
item.description: - Changes at Google DeepMind: Hassabis to Chair, Jeff Dean departs: A surprising leadership shakeup at the peak of Google's AI momentum raises questions about what's really happening behind the scenes. (https://blog.google/company-news/inside-google/message-ceo/next-chapter-ai-momentum/) - DeepSeek planning to significantly raise prices: The AI disruptor famous for dirt-cheap models is about to prove that cheap AI was never actually free. (https://platform.deepseek.com/usage) - Humans missed 1 in 3 threats approving AI agent commands across 40k game runs: A wild new stat shows human oversight of AI agents might be more theater than safety net. (https://scalex.dev/blog/ai-agent-permissions-stats/) - Discovery Loop: The addictive new curiosity rabbit-hole site that ate Hacker News' entire day. (https://www.discoveryloop.com/) - Crime Pays but Botany Doesn't: A botanist's reading list on why plant science gets no love became an unlikely hit — and a metaphor for underfunded, unglamorous work everywhere. (https://www.crimepaysbutbotanydoesnt.com/reading-list)

item.title: Drive Radio — August 7, 2026
item.description: - US strikes $1.2B deal to pay German firm to halt offshore wind projects: The government paid nine figures just to make sure a wind farm never gets built — a wild snapshot of current energy politics. (https://www.bbc.com/news/articles/c1e1vg0gjl5o) - Mario Meets Pareto: A viral deep-dive applies the 80/20 rule to Super Mario level design and accidentally explains why some games just feel better. (https://www.mayerowitz.io/blog/mario-meets-pareto) - AMD acquires Taalas to boost inference performance by etching models in silicon: AMD's buying a startup that literally burns AI models into chips — a bold bet on speed over flexibility. (https://www.theregister.com/systems/2026/08/06/amd-acquires-ai-chip-startup-taalas-to-boost-inference-performance-by-etching-models-into-silicon/5284344) - New Mexico court orders Meta to pay $567m over harms to children's mental health: A landmark ruling that's small money for Meta but potentially huge legal precedent. (https://www.theguardian.com/technology/2026/aug/06/new-mexico-court-meta) - Radical Study Suggests Life on Earth Arose Twice: New research suggests life may have sparked from non-living matter more than once — reshaping how we think about life elsewhere in the universe. (https://www.sciencealert.com/radical-study-suggests-life-on-earth-arose-from-non-living-matter-twice) - U.S. economy lost 23,000 jobs in July, a sudden reversal: A confusing jobs report where the headline number and the real story point in opposite directions. (https://www.nbcnews.com/business/economy/july-2026-jobs-report-rcna591138)

item.title: Drive Radio — August 8, 2026
item.description: - Now we have a timeline of the OpenAI accidental attack against Hugging Face: A forensic timeline reveals how an autonomous OpenAI system accidentally DDoS'd Hugging Face — a scary preview of machine-speed mistakes with no human in the loop. (https://simonwillison.net/2026/Aug/7/openai-timeline/) - New Amazon Data Center Is Set to Have the Most Polluting Power Plant in the U.S.: The AI boom's carbon cost just got a literal address, as Amazon pairs a new Texas data center with what could be the country's dirtiest power plant. (https://www.nytimes.com/2026/08/08/climate/amazon-data-center-texas-pollution.html) - The Nixpkgs core team has disbanded: The volunteer team steering NixOS's massive package ecosystem just walked away, exposing how fragile open-source infrastructure really is. (https://discourse.nixos.org/t/the-nixpkgs-core-team-has-disbanded/79413) - Hardware backdoors in some x86 CPUs: Researchers exposed a hidden, undocumented processor core in certain x86 chips that can bypass all normal security — a literal backdoor in silicon. (https://github.com/xoreaxeaxeax/rosenbridge) - DeepMind's WeatherNext model achieves breakthrough forecasting cyclones: AI is now beating traditional physics models at predicting cyclone paths, giving coastal communities crucial extra days of warning. (https://deepmind.google/blog/weathernext-ai-model-achieves-breakthrough-in-forecasting-cyclones/) - NASA figured out how to keep its Voyager 2 probe running for another year: Forty-eight years and twelve billion miles from home, Voyager 2 gets one more clever power trick to keep phoning Earth. (https://www.space.com/space-exploration/voyager/nasa-figured-out-how-to-keep-its-48-year-old-voyager-2-probe-running-for-yet-another-year)

item.title: Drive Radio — August 9, 2026
item.description: - My server is a phone now: A dead Android phone gets a second life as a full-blown home server, battery and all — the ultimate e-waste hack. (https://seg6.space/posts/phone-server/) - _for-sale DNS records: A quietly clever new DNS record lets domain owners advertise 'this is for sale' directly in the internet's plumbing. (https://specification.website/spec/foundations/for-sale-dns/) - CSS: The bomb inside your inbox: Turns out the 'harmless' styling language can crash mail clients and leak data — no JavaScript required. (https://portswigger.net/research/css-the-bomb-inside-your-inbox) - Amazon circumvents Gilroy community vote for AI data center: A 45-year-old procedural rule lets Amazon sidestep public comment on a massive new AI data center. (https://www.tomshardware.com/tech-industry/data-centers/amazon-secretly-circumvents-community-vote-for-massive-ai-data-center-45-year-old-rules-lock-gilroy-residents-out-of-public-comment-window) - Everything You Do Is Being Recorded: AI wearables are creating a new always-listening reality — and a whole new etiquette war around it. (https://www.theatlantic.com/technology/2026/05/ai-wearable-surveillance-countermeasures/687203/)

item.title: Drive Radio — August 10, 2026
item.description: - Taxi drivers rarely die of Alzheimer's: A wild dive into how spatial navigation physically grows the hippocampus — and what GPS-dependence might be doing to our brains. (https://theconversation.com/taxi-drivers-rarely-die-of-alzheimers-how-complex-mental-maps-and-spatial-reasoning-protect-your-brain-286650) - Over 181,000 AI meeting recordings left wide open: An exposed backend at a popular AI note-taker shows how fast 'convenient' AI tools can turn into a massive privacy leak. (https://bobdahacker.com/blog/tldv-hack) - 50k Boat Names: A delightfully pointless dataset of tens of thousands of real boat names, because not every story needs a moral. (https://www.beautifulpublicdata.com/boat-names/) - Docker Sandboxes: Docker's new disposable environments for AI agents signal a big shift: infrastructure built to contain code written by AI, not humans. (https://www.docker.com/products/docker-sandboxes/) - Because It's Not Fun Enough: why languages fail: A sharp argument that programming languages succeed or die based on how fun they are to use, not how technically sound they are. (https://bytecode.news/posts/2026/08/because-it-s-not-fun-enough)

item.title: Drive Radio — August 11, 2026
item.description: - France to ban unsolicited telemarketing calls: France is flipping the default so companies need your consent before cold-calling you, with fines up to €75,000 per violation. (https://www.lemonde.fr/en/france/article/2026/08/06/france-to-ban-unsolicited-telemarketing-calls-from-august-11_6756208_7.html) - Mark Zuckerberg attacks 'closed' AI rivals as Meta returns to open models: Meta is betting that open-weight AI commoditizes its rivals' moats, right as it pushes its new always-on local agent model Muse Glimmer. (https://www.ft.com/content/4e3957f8-ea7c-4c46-a3de-cdce8e526878) - Muse Glimmer: 30B-parameter model optimized for always-on local agent workflows: Meta's new open model is designed to live on your device as a persistent AI agent — useful or unsettling, take your pick. (https://research.meta.ai/blog/introducing-muse-glimmer-open-agentic-model) - As AI eats the web, the internet's collective memory is disappearing: AI answers are starving the websites they were trained on of traffic, and the sites — and the knowledge on them — are quietly vanishing. (https://thewalrus.ca/google-search-is-dying/) - England set to be one of the first countries to eliminate hepatitis C: No vaccine, no miracle drug — just relentless testing and antivirals, and it's actually working at a national scale. (https://www.bbc.com/news/articles/c75gk620r22o) - What I learned by putting GitHub Copilot behind a MitM proxy: Turns out your AI coding assistant is shipping a lot more of your codebase back home than most developers realize. (https://www.lighthousenewsletter.com/p/i-put-github-copilot-behind-a-mitm)

item.title: Drive Radio — August 13, 2026
item.description: - PBS loses access to 70 years of TV archives after cloud vendor goes defunct: A vendor collapse — not a hack — locked PBS out of 50TB of irreplaceable archival footage, and now they're suing just to get into the room. (https://www.tomshardware.com/software/cloud-storage/nine-pbs-loses-access-to-70-years-of-data-after-contracted-cloud-storage-vendor-goes-defunct-public-tv-channel-sues-iron-mountain-data-center-which-hosts-archival-materials-to-ensure-preservation) - Tracking down the 16-year-old WAL-reset SQLite bug: Tailscale engineers hunted down a subtle bug hiding in the world's most deployed database for over a decade. (https://tailscale.com/blog/sqlite-wal-reset-bug) - DeepSeek Harness, API Pricing Update, and V4 Pro buzz: DeepSeek dominated the news cycle in one day with a new agent harness, updated pricing, and a trending next-gen model. (https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) - Qwen3.8-2.4T: A new 2.4-trillion-parameter model release shows the AI scale race is nowhere near slowing down. (https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen3.8-2.4T-A95B) - Choosing an AI model: one prompt, 11 models, different results: Netlify's experiment reveals just how differently AI models 'think' even when given the exact same instructions. (https://www.netlify.com/blog/one-prompt-11-models-very-different-results/) - Rapid warming may tip AMOC at 2°C, slower warming may avert collapse: New research suggests the speed of warming — not just the total amount — could determine whether a critical ocean current system collapses. (https://phys.org/news/2026-08-rapid-atlantic-circulation-2c-slower.html)

item.title: Drive Radio — August 14, 2026
item.description: - Spaghettifying DRAM: A Rowhammer-style memory attack technique with a black-hole physics name, and a reminder that denser chips are also easier to exploit. (https://github.com/xoreaxeaxeax/skitter-creek-bath-salts) - Accelerating GPT-5.6 Sol Ultrafast: Cerebras and OpenAI team up to make inference absurdly fast, quietly building the plumbing for chatty AI agents. (https://www.cerebras.ai/blog/accelerating-gpt-5-6-sol-ultrafast-with-openai) - France's tax authority had data stolen on 680k taxpayers: A massive breach of French tax records shows legacy government systems remain the real weak point, not flashy AI threats. (https://korben.info/en/france-tax-authority-data-breach-680000-taxpayers.html) - GLM-5.3: Frontier coding with emergent cyber capabilities: A major AI lab openly markets its model's surprise hacking skills as a feature. (https://z.ai/blog/glm-5.3) - DeepSeek peak/off-peak pricing update: DeepSeek starts pricing AI compute like electricity, with peak and off-peak rates. (https://api-docs.deepseek.com/news/news260813/) - Why does Opus 5 feel worse to work with?: A viral post argues newer AI models trade collaborative charm for benchmark-chasing caution. (https://mun-logadan.github.io/why-does-opus-5-feel-worse/)

item.title: Drive Radio — August 15, 2026
item.description: - Firefox is now the last major browser that still supports uBlock Origin: Chrome's ad-blocker crackdown just handed Firefox its biggest competitive edge in years. (https://www.pcworld.com/article/3212428/firefox-is-now-the-last-major-browser-that-still-supports-ublock-origin.html) - Qwen 3.8 27B: A new open-weight model is closing the gap with frontier AI labs, and developers can run it themselves. (https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B-FP8) - Google is making private AI practical with homomorphic encryption: Google claims it can now run AI on your data without ever decrypting it — a wild pivot for an ad company. (https://blog.google/security/how-google-is-making-private-ai-practical-with-homomorphic-encryption/) - Going Dark, and the era of law enforcement hacking: As encryption gets stronger, law enforcement has quietly shifted from cracking codes to hacking phones directly. (https://blog.cryptographyengineering.com/2026/08/14/everything-is-about-to-go-dark/) - Strait of Hormuz Live Traffic Tracking: A hobbyist built a real-time dashboard for the waterway that a fifth of the world's oil flows through. (https://hormuz.now/) - Auto-research with codex: How I achieved a 232x Faster Kernel: One developer let an AI run overnight optimization experiments on its own code and got a 232x speedup. (https://sankalp.bearblog.dev/autoresearch/)

item.title: Drive Radio — August 16, 2026
item.description: - Asus Bike Booster: A motherboard company just launched a clip-on e-bike turbocharger, and the internet can't decide if it's genius or absurd. (https://www.asus.com/accessories/bike-booster/asus-oxiis/oxiis-intelligent-bike-booster/) - Semaglutide linked to lower predicted dementia risk: The Ozempic-class drugs might be doing more than shrinking waistlines — early data hints at a brain benefit too. (https://alz-journals.onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.1002/dad2.70432) - RISC-V: They Should Have Known Better: A veteran chip engineer argues the 'open' future of computing repeated the exact design mistakes it was supposed to avoid. (https://dmitry.gr/?r=06.%20Thoughts&proj=12.%20RV) - Super El Niño Keeps Growing: Forecasters say this winter's El Niño is climbing toward historic territory, with real consequences for weather across three continents. (https://www.severe-weather.eu/long-range-2/super-el-nino-growth-accelerating-to-record-strength-fall-winter-2026-2027-forecast-impact-united-states-canada-europe-fa/) - At-home test for infected ticks: A new rapid test lets you check whether the tick that bit you actually carries Lyme disease, instead of waiting days for a lab. (https://www.smithsonianmag.com/innovation/the-first-at-home-test-for-infected-ticks-could-improve-lyme-disease-diagnosis-180989235/)

item.title: Drive Radio — August 17, 2026
item.description: - Stripe to Buy OpenRouter for $7B: Stripe isn't just processing payments anymore — it's buying the switchboard that routes AI API calls across every model provider. (https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2026-08-16/stripe-nears-deal-to-buy-ai-firm-openrouter-for-over-7-billion) - The AI Credit Resale Economy: A gray market of 'token brokers' is buying and reselling discounted AI API credits, revealing just how hungry the world is for cheap inference. (https://vectoral.com/blog/who-are-the-token-brokers) - Tell HN: GitHub Is Overloaded: A minor outage that's a good reminder how much of the software world depends on one company's servers staying up. (https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=49330597) - Self hosted email continues to steeply decline: A deep dive into the top million domains shows self-hosted email is basically dead, crushed under spam filters favoring Google and Microsoft. (https://labs.ripe.net/author/artem-berezin/two-providers-a-stubborn-plateau-and-a-very-long-tail-email-in-the-tranco-top-1m/) - Cialis is an erectile dysfunction drug. Could it also help you live longer?: New research links tadalafil to heart health and longevity benefits well beyond its original purpose. (https://www.npr.org/2026/08/17/nx-s1-5928263/cialis-viagra-tadalafil-longevity-heart-health) - Anthropic's 'watermark' text adulteration in Claude is a perversion of writing: Claude is reportedly altering its own word choices as a hidden watermark, sparking a fight over who really controls AI-generated text. (https://daringfireball.net/2026/08/anthropics_watermark_text_adulteration_in_claude_is_a_perversion_of_writing)
